 Patriot League football: Lehigh looks to rebound from first loss at Villanova

 Lehigh’s Luke Yoder runs the ball against Villanova during a playoff football game Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025, at Lehigh’s Goodman Stadium in Bethlehem. (Jonathan Broady/Special to The Morning Call)
 By Keith Groller | kgroller@mcall.com | The Morning Call PUBLISHED: October 23, 2026 at 12:14 PM EDT Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... What happened?
 Lehigh football coach Rich Nagy was probably asked that question in the last few days more than he’d care to remember.
 Nagy suffered his first loss as the Mountain Hawks coach and the team lost a regular season game for the first time since 2024 when it fell 48-38 at Cornell.
 While there are no easy explanations for what happened in upstate New York, there is an easy way to stop the question from being asked and that’s to beat Villanova at 3:30 p.m. Saturday in suburban Philadelphia.
 The loss at Cornell may have knocked Lehigh from No. 4 in the FCS national polls to No. 11 in one and No. 12 in another, it didn’t ruin the team’s hopes for a third straight Patriot League title.
 The Mountain Hawks have yet to lose in the league this season, but know that this will be their biggest challenge to date in facing a Wildcats team that may be the best 3-4 squad in the country.
 Villanova has beaten Lehigh 12 consecutive times, including a 14-7 win at Goodman Stadium last December in the FCS playoffs in a game that was agonizing for local fans because Lehigh outgained the Wildcats 339-235, including 178-27 on the gorund.
 The last time the Mountain Hawks beat the Wildcats was 2006 and it was the late Andy Coen’s first win as Lehigh coach.
 If there is a good way to bounce back from your first loss, for Nagy’s team it’s by beating Villanova.
 As for what happened at Cornell to a defense that had been ranked in several national categories coming in, Nagy said the team had a slow start that dug a big hole it couldn’t escape.
 “We obviously didn’t start very well,” Nagy said. “We come out in the first half and only get about six yards on offense and gave up about 300 yards. Fortunately, we got that 100-yard fumble recovery for a touchdown that helped keep us in the game, but for whatever reason we just didn’t start well. I give our kids a lot of credit for fighting back. They never gave up. We got it to a seven-point game several times, but we just couldn’t overcome that last obstacle.”
 In looking back on last week coming off the bye, Nagy said: “I thought we were prepared. But those things happen. Give Cornell credit because they are a good football team. They made some plays and we didn’t. We didn’t respond well to the situation. Once we got going, I thought we did well and you hope that it’s a good growth experience for us moving forward.”
 Nagy is confident his team will respond.
 “We have a lot of competitive guys which is why you saw the fight we showed,” he said. “But at the same time, we have to look at ourselves and it starts with me. We have to do a better job of being more prepared to begin that game than we were. Sometimes you get yourself in a situation that you can’t get out of. That’s what happened. Just like we do when we win, we look back and address the problems and go over the goods and the bads and move forward, asking ourselves, ‘How do we get better?’ “
 Villanova was blown out by FBS opponent Louisville 59-13, but it’s other three losses are by seven points or less.
 Nagy said that the respect for the Wildcats has always been there.
 “Since we came here as a staff in 2023, we looked at Villanova as the premier FCS program on the East Coast,” he said. “That’s the team we studied and that’s the team we knew we had to emulate if we wanted to get Lehigh to where we want to be. There are a lot of similarities between the two programs. We played Villanova in our first game here in 2023 and got beat decisively [38-10]. But from that first meeting to playing them in the playoffs last year, there was marked improvement. We had a chance to win, but at the end of the day we knew we were competing with them and we knew we had an opportunity.”
 Nagy said it’s no different this week.
 “We’re going to get a chance to play and there’s the benchmark of where they have been and where want to go,” Nagy said. “That benchmark is going to be there until we beat them. We understand that. It has been 20 years, and I remember coaching against them when I was at Maine. Villanova has always had good teams and they have a great history, a great tradition, the whole thing. If you want to be the best in your league, and they are the best around, you’ve got to go out and beat them.”
 Lehigh (6-1, 4-0 Patriot) at Villanova (3-4, 2-2)
 When/where: 3:30 p.m. Saturday at Villanova Stadium.
 The storylines: This is the first Patriot League meeting between these two Eastern Pennsylvania programs only about an hour’s drive apart. Lehigh is looking to bounce back, especially on defense, after giving up 600 yards of offense at Cornell. Villanova, 0-3 at home so far this season, is trying to stay in the Patriot League race with a game at Lafayette coming up next week. These are the top two offenses in the league in both scoring offense and total offense. Lehigh suffered a major loss when all-league safety Nick Peltekian went out with an injury at Cornell and didn’t return. His status for this one is uncertain, although he was still listed as the starter on the depth chart released by the school.
 Players to watch: Sophomore quarterback Derek Morgan threw three touchdown passes at Cornell and Luke Yoder had another big rushing day. He needs just 44 yards to reach 1,000 in a season for the third time in his career. The key will be the defense, which was allowing 11.8 points per game before giving up 48 at Cornell, including 234 yards rushing. Junior safety Luke Denny, who had the 100-yard fumble return for a touchdown, will play a key role against Villanova. First-year player Cayden Vassa, a Bethlehem Catholic graduate, is also expected to see a lot of action. He had nine tackles at Cornell. The Wildcats are led by quarterback Pat McQuaide, who threw for 235 yards and two TDs in a win over Fordham last week. Isaiah Ragland and Ja’briel Mace both had rushing TDs against Fordham and are over 400 yards on the season. Omari Bursey is the team’s top tackler with 77 stops.
 Keith Groller’s pick: Lehigh 26-21
